answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must continually answer randomly timed challenges and publish a signed heartbeat; the ledger accumulates an unbroken attention history that decays whenever a challenge is missed. A duplicate account starts cold at dawn with zero history, so it cannot borrow the standing of an older account. Cross-account reuse of response patterns trips a ridge threshold and freezes the cluster. The attacker’s cost is the sustained labor of keeping every fake identity continuously responsive, and a single missed window buries that identity as a dead relic.
